name: Pegylated Liposomal DOXOrubicin for Kaposi Sarcoma
cyclesNote: continue per response and tolerance; not a fixed cycle count (source states every 2 to 3 weeks)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Kaposi sarcoma is HHV-8 (human herpesvirus-8) driven; this cytotoxic regimen is not molecular-biomarker-restricted. In AIDS-related (HIV-associated) Kaposi sarcoma, optimizing antiretroviral therapy (ART) is foundational and is given alongside systemic chemotherapy. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Kaposi Sarcoma v2.2026, Systemic Therapy Dosing (KS-A).

histology: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8/human herpesvirus-8 driven vascular neoplasm)
supportiveCare: optimize antiretroviral therapy (ART) in HIV-associated Kaposi sarcoma; involve infectious disease as needed.
cardiac surveillance: echocardiogram before the initial course of liposomal doxorubicin and periodically; consider limiting lifetime dose (NCCN Kaposi footnote d, line 980).
monitor for infusion reactions and palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia characteristic of pegylated liposomal doxorubicin.
monitor for neutropenia; G-CSF per febrile-neutropenia risk, especially in AIDS-related disease.
SOURCED ALTERNATIVE first-line agent: Paclitaxel 60 mg/m2 weekly, 100 mg/m2 every 2 weeks, 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks, or 135 mg/m2 every 3 weeks (NCCN Kaposi v2.2026, line 923 to 926).
monitoring: cardiac function (echocardiogram before initial course and periodically)
HIV viral load and CD4 count and ART adherence in AIDS-related disease

doseModificationRules.text: Hold and obtain cardiology review; consider limiting lifetime cumulative dose per NCCN footnote d (line 980).

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 to 4 palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia or neutropenia
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume at a reduced dose or lengthened interval per labeling and clinical review.

drugs.name: Pegylated liposomal DOXOrubicin
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Kaposi Sarcoma v2.2026, First-Line Systemic Therapy Dosing (KS-A), line 921 to 922. Pegylated liposomal DOXOrubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2 to 3 weeks (cycleLengthDays modeled as 21 with a 14 to 21 day source-stated interval). DISTINCT ANTHRACYCLINE PROFILE: pegylated liposomal doxorubicin has different pharmacokinetics and a lower per-cycle cardiotoxicity profile than conventional doxorubicin, so the conventional free-doxorubicin cumulative 450/550 mg/m2 ceiling does NOT translate directly; caps.perDose and cumulativeLifetime are left null. Instead, per NCCN footnote d (line 980), perform echocardiography before the initial course and periodically and consider limiting the lifetime dose. ISMP tall-man applied (DOXOrubicin). AIDS context: give with optimized ART; low-grade neutropenia is the common toxicity in HIV-associated disease. ALTERNATIVE first-line option: Paclitaxel, dose-schedule options 60 mg/m2 IV weekly, 100 mg/m2 IV every 2 weeks, 100 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks, or 135 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks (line 923 to 926), modeled here as a sourced note rather than a separate drug.

provenance.locator: First-Line Systemic Therapy Dosing (KS-A): Liposomal Doxorubicin 20 mg/m2 IV every 2 to 3 weeks (line 921 to 922); cardiotoxicity footnote d (echocardiogram before initial course and periodically; consider limiting lifetime dose) (line 980)
